quests.instruction: Complete the sentence: “Flying to the next town by plane is possible, but flying to the Moon in a paper plane is…”
quests.hint: Could any paper plane really make that trip?
quests.explanation: Possible means something can happen. Impossible means it can’t happen at all.
quests.funFact: Paper planes can glide for a surprisingly long time, but only because of the air around them.

quests.instruction: Which sentence describes the opposite of “The street was busy and bright at noon”?
quests.correctAnswer: The street was quiet and dark at midnight.
options: The street was busy and bright at midnight.
The street was quiet and dark at midnight.
The street was quiet and bright at noon.
quests.hint: Change both the time and the mood of the street.
quests.explanation: Noon belongs to the day, and midnight belongs to the night. Both the time and the feel of the street flip.
quests.funFact: Many cities leave street lights on all night so people can see.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “Everyone walked in through the front gate”?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone walked out through the front gate.
options: Everyone walked in through the back gate.
Everyone ran in through the front gate.
Everyone walked out through the front gate.
quests.hint: Only one word needs to change to reverse the direction.
quests.explanation: Walking in means entering. Walking out means leaving. The other choices change the speed or the gate, not the direction.
quests.funFact: The word “gate” is related to an old word for an opening or a way through.

quests.instruction: It’s the middle of the dry season and there isn’t a single cloud in the sky, so rain today is very…
quests.hint: What are the chances when the sky is perfectly clear?
quests.explanation: Likely means it will probably happen. Unlikely means it probably won’t.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasters often give rain chances as percentages.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence with the opposite meaning: “Dad left the porch light on all night.”
quests.correctAnswer: Dad left the porch light off all night.
options: Dad left the porch light off all night.
Dad left the porch door open all night.
Dad left the porch light on until dawn.
quests.hint: Picture the porch after dark.
quests.explanation: On means switched to work, and off means switched not to. Only one choice reverses just that.
quests.funFact: Porch lights are often used to make a house easier to find after dark.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the opposite idea: “Grandpa’s watch is old and scratched, but the one on Aarav’s wrist is…”
quests.hint: Picture a watch just out of its box.
quests.explanation: Old things have been used for a long time. New things have just arrived.
quests.funFact: The first wristwatches were made for women in the 1800s, and many men only began wearing them later.

quests.instruction: Finding a coin on the way to school felt lucky. Dropping the bag of marbles right before the bell felt…
quests.hint: How would you feel about the marbles bouncing everywhere?
quests.explanation: Lucky means good things happen by chance. Unlucky means the chance goes the wrong way.
quests.funFact: Four-leaf clovers are rare, which is why many people see them as lucky.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the opposite of “thick”: “The dosa batter is too thick, so Amma adds water to make it…”
quests.hint: Which way would you move the batter by adding water?
quests.explanation: Thick batter barely flows. Adding water makes it thinner and easier to spread.
quests.funFact: Dosa batter is made from rice and lentils that are soaked, ground and left to ferment.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “The bus stopped at the corner”?
quests.correctAnswer: The bus started moving from the corner.
options: The bus started moving from the corner.
The bus parked at the corner.
The bus waited at the corner.
quests.hint: Waiting and parking are both kinds of stopping.
quests.explanation: The opposite of stopping is setting off again. “Waited” and “parked” still mean not moving.
quests.funFact: The first bus services began in the early 1800s.

quests.instruction: A torch is useful on a dark road. A torch with no battery is…
quests.hint: What can a torch do without power?
quests.explanation: Useful things help you do something. Useless things don’t help at all.
quests.funFact: Many everyday things, like the zip, were invented to solve one small problem.

quests.instruction: Which sentence says the opposite of “The twins wore the same dress”?
quests.hint: Twins in matching outfits are wearing the same thing.
quests.explanation: The same means exactly alike. Different means not alike. “Matching” still means alike.
quests.funFact: Identical twins share nearly the same genes, but each has their own fingerprints.

quests.instruction: A tidy desk has pencils in a box. Which description matches the opposite?
quests.correctAnswer: Pencils, papers and crumbs spread across the whole desk
options: Pencils lined up neatly beside the notebook
Pencils, papers and crumbs spread across the whole desk
Books stacked in a tall, straight pile
quests.hint: Think of a desk where you couldn’t find a pencil.
quests.explanation: Tidy means neat and organized. Messy means scattered and disorderly.
quests.funFact: Many people say a clear desk helps them find things faster.

quests.instruction: Having a big garden is an advantage for a dog. Having to mow it every week is a ___ for the family.
quests.hint: What does the dog get that the family doesn’t enjoy?
quests.explanation: An advantage is a helpful point. A disadvantage is a point that causes trouble.
quests.funFact: Pros-and-cons lists help people compare advantages and disadvantages.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “Our team won the final”?
quests.hint: Playing and reaching the final don’t say who came out on top.
quests.explanation: The opposite of winning is losing. The other choices don’t tell you the result at all.
quests.funFact: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

quests.instruction: The little girl laughed when the balloon floated up. Which choice shows the opposite reaction when it floated away?
quests.hint: Laughing is happy. What is the opposite reaction?
quests.explanation: Laughing is a happy sound and crying is a sad one, so they show opposite feelings.
quests.funFact: Babies cry to tell people they need something.

quests.instruction: A raincoat is necessary on a stormy day. On a bright, hot afternoon, it’s…
quests.hint: Would you need it to stay dry?
quests.explanation: Necessary means you can’t do without it. Unnecessary means you don’t need it.
quests.funFact: Packing lists help travelers bring what’s necessary and leave out what isn’t.

quests.instruction: Which sentence says the opposite of “The bird flew above the clouds”?
quests.correctAnswer: The bird flew below the clouds.
options: The bird flew beside the clouds.
The bird flew toward the clouds.
The bird flew below the clouds.
quests.hint: “Higher than” becomes “lower than”.
quests.explanation: Above means higher than, and below means lower than. “Beside” and “toward” don’t flip the position.
quests.funFact: Some birds, like geese, can fly higher than most small planes.

quests.instruction: Which sentence shows the opposite movement from “Dad stepped forward to pick up the ball”?
quests.correctAnswer: Dad stepped back to avoid the ball.
options: Dad stepped up to catch the ball.
Dad stepped aside to pass the ball.
Dad stepped back to avoid the ball.
quests.hint: Think about the direction of Dad’s feet.
quests.explanation: Forward goes toward what’s ahead; backward goes away from it. “Up” and “aside” aren’t the reverse.
quests.funFact: Footballs were once made from animal bladders covered in leather.

quests.instruction: At the market, Meena buys vegetables grown in nearby villages. They’re local. The apples flown in from another continent are…
quests.hint: Where were they grown, close by or far away?
quests.explanation: Local means from nearby. Foreign means from another country or place far away.
quests.funFact: Many shops now label food with the country where it was grown.

quests.instruction: Which sentence describes the opposite of “The puppy ran toward the gate”?
quests.correctAnswer: The puppy ran away from the gate.
options: The puppy ran around the gate.
The puppy jumped over the gate.
The puppy ran away from the gate.
quests.hint: Picture the puppy with the gate behind it.
quests.explanation: Toward means closer, and away from means farther. “Around” and “over” still involve the gate.
quests.funFact: Dogs can run faster over short distances than most people can.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that means the opposite of “The whole class is healthy this week”.
quests.correctAnswer: Everybody in the class is sick this week.
options: Everybody in the class is sick this week.
Everybody in the class is busy this week.
Nobody in the class is here this week.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that changes only how the children feel.
quests.explanation: Healthy means well, and sick means unwell. The other sentences don’t describe health.
quests.funFact: Vaccines help the body get ready to fight certain illnesses.

quests.instruction: From the plane window, the houses below looked tiny. Standing next to the plane on the runway, the wing looked…
quests.hint: What changes when you go from far away to very close?
quests.explanation: Tiny means extremely small and huge means extremely large. The size looks different when you’re close.
quests.funFact: A big jet’s wings can be longer than a basketball court.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “The clock is broken, so it always shows 3:00”?
quests.correctAnswer: The clock is fixed, so it shows the right time.
options: The clock is loud, so it always wakes me.
The clock is old, so it shows the time slowly.
The clock is fixed, so it shows the right time.
quests.hint: Picture a clock you could finally trust.
quests.explanation: Broken means not working. Fixed means working properly again.
quests.funFact: Clocks with pendulums were among the first very accurate timekeepers.

quests.instruction: Which sentence shows the opposite of “Hari did the puzzle alone”?
quests.correctAnswer: Hari and his cousins did the puzzle together.
options: Hari and his cousins did the puzzle together.
quests.hint: Count the people at the puzzle table.
quests.explanation: Alone means with no one else; together means with others. The other choices say nothing about company.
quests.funFact: The jigsaw puzzle is thought to have started as a teaching tool for maps.

quests.instruction: A recipe for 4 people uses 2 cups of rice. For 8 people, you need double. For just 2 people, you need ___ of the original.
quests.hint: If the number of people is cut in two, what happens to the rice?
quests.explanation: Double means twice as much, and half means one of two equal parts.
quests.funFact: “Half” is spelled with a silent letter l.

quests.instruction: Which sentence says the opposite of “Kavi lost his keys at the park”?
quests.correctAnswer: Kavi found his keys at the park.
options: Kavi found his keys at the park.
Kavi dropped his keys at the park.
Kavi kept his keys at the park.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that ends with the keys back in his hand.
quests.explanation: Losing is no longer having something; finding is having it again. “Dropped” might be how they were lost.
quests.funFact: Many train stations keep a room full of lost umbrellas and bags.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “The water in the kettle was boiling”?
quests.correctAnswer: The water in the bucket was freezing.
options: The water in the bucket was freezing.
The water in the kettle was bubbling.
The water in the bucket was warm.
quests.hint: Think of the opposite extreme of boiling.
quests.explanation: Boiling is the extreme hot end; freezing is the extreme cold end. “Warm” sits between them.
quests.funFact: Water can exist as a solid, a liquid and a gas.

quests.instruction: The soup tasted bland because the cook added hardly any salt. Another cook added a whole handful, so it had ___ salt.
quests.hint: Is salt something you count or something you measure?
quests.explanation: Too little means not enough, and too much means more than you need. “Much” goes with things you can’t count one by one.
quests.funFact: Your body needs a little salt, but too much can be bad for you.

quests.instruction: The teacher counted 31 books for 30 students, so one was extra. The next week she counted only 29, so one was…
quests.hint: Compare the number of books with the number of students.
quests.explanation: Extra means more than needed. Missing means one or more are gone.
quests.funFact: “Extra” comes from a Latin word meaning “outside” or “beyond”.

quests.instruction: After days of non-stop rain, the river burst its banks in a flood. After months without a drop, the land cracked open in a…
quests.hint: Think of land cracked open after months without rain.
quests.explanation: A flood is too much water. A drought is a long period with too little.
quests.funFact: Rice is often grown in flooded fields called paddies.
